ramparts.title: Ramparts & Great Gate
ramparts.lead: Kilometres of ochre walls that earned Taroudant the nickname "little Marrakech".
ramparts.overview: The ochre earthen ramparts circle the whole medina and change colour with the light. Walk, cycle or take a horse-drawn calèche along them; the great gate is the easiest landmark for entering the old town.
ramparts.visit: Allow 1–2 hours for a partial loop; the light is best late in the afternoon.
ramparts.tip: Agree the calèche price before you board.

bab-el-kasbah.title: Bab El Kasbah
bab-el-kasbah.lead: A monumental gate opening onto the kasbah quarter, in the heart of the old town.
bab-el-kasbah.overview: One of the most photographed gates of the walls, surrounded by small cafés and workshops. It leads to the kasbah quarter, calmer than the souks.
bab-el-kasbah.visit: A 15–30 minute stop while moving between souks.
bab-el-kasbah.tip: Come early morning or at dusk for the best photos.

souk-arabe.title: Arab Souk
souk-arabe.lead: The everyday souk: spices, argan, clothing and hardware.
souk-arabe.overview: The Arab souk is the busiest market in the medina. You will find spices, argan oil, clothes, slippers and everyday goods, in a less touristy atmosphere than Marrakech.
souk-arabe.visit: Allow 1–2 hours; mornings and late afternoons are liveliest.
souk-arabe.tip: Haggle with a smile and compare two or three stalls before buying.

souk-berbere.title: Berber (Amazigh) Souk
souk-berbere.lead: Jewellery, carpets, pottery and Amazigh crafts from the Souss.
souk-berbere.overview: The Berber, or Amazigh, souk is the craft corner: silver jewellery, carpets, pottery and decorative objects from the Souss region. A good place for souvenirs that last.
souk-berbere.visit: About 1 hour; take time to talk with the artisans.
souk-berbere.tip: Ask where pieces come from and compare before buying antique jewellery.

place-assarag.title: Assarag Square (20 August Square)
place-assarag.lead: The big lively square of the medina, a local meeting point.
place-assarag.overview: Surrounded by cafés and small restaurants, Assarag Square is the heart of local life. Sit on a terrace and watch the town go by, especially toward the end of the day.
place-assarag.visit: A one-hour break over tea or a meal; liveliest in the evening.
place-assarag.tip: Ask prices before ordering on terraces.

tanneries.title: Traditional Tanneries
tanneries.lead: Hand leatherwork, best visited with a guide or a local.
tanneries.overview: Taroudant's tanneries are smaller and calmer than Fes's. You can watch the stages of leather work, from raw hide to the dye pits.
tanneries.visit: 30 minutes to 1 hour; smells are strong, especially in summer.
tanneries.tip: Ask permission before taking photos and agree any tip in advance.

palais-claudio-bravo.title: Claudio Bravo Palace
palais-claudio-bravo.lead: The palace associated with the Chilean painter Claudio Bravo, who settled in Taroudant.
palais-claudio-bravo.overview: Claudio Bravo, a Chilean painter based in Taroudant, left a palace noted for its architecture and gardens. It now also welcomes guests as a hotel with a pool, garden and restaurant, so check access and visiting conditions before you go.
palais-claudio-bravo.visit: Allow 30–60 minutes if a visit is possible; check access beforehand.
palais-claudio-bravo.tip: Ask locally or call ahead before making the trip.

jardin-roudani.title: Roudani Garden (Dona)
jardin-roudani.lead: A calm green break in the middle of town.
jardin-roudani.overview: Roudani Garden offers shade and quiet between souk visits. It is a simple place to rest, especially in the hottest hours.
jardin-roudani.tip: Come during the hot hours to enjoy the shade.

place-al-alaouiyine.title: Al Alaouiyine Square
place-al-alaouiyine.lead: An open square lined with cafés, ideal for a break between visits.
place-al-alaouiyine.overview: Al Alaouiyine Square is airier than the souks, with cafés and small restaurants. It works as a landmark and meeting point.
place-al-alaouiyine.visit: A 30–60 minute break, by day or in the evening.
place-al-alaouiyine.tip: A good start or end point for a walk around the ramparts.

oasis-tiout.title: Tiout Oasis
oasis-tiout.lead: A palm grove and an old kasbah about 30 km away, for a half-day in nature.
oasis-tiout.overview: The Tiout oasis, in the Souss valley, combines palm trees, orchards and an old kasbah. It is the classic excursion from Taroudant for a change from the medina.
oasis-tiout.visit: Allow half a day including the trip; a taxi or car with driver is best.
oasis-tiout.tip: Leave in the morning and agree the round-trip price with the driver in advance.
